page: Microsoft Azure HB368-96rs_v5 is a high-performance computing server instance built upon an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. The platform provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 448 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced density of approximately 4.67 GB per core. As a member of the HBv5 family, the underlying hardware is structured specifically for parallel processing requirements that demand deterministic, non-oversubscribed CPU access.

The instance bundles an extensive 15,875 GB local NVMe SSD storage array, providing high direct storage capacity and rapid read-write speeds without needing immediate external volumes, although Premium Storage integration remains supported. Networking capabilities include RDMA support, facilitating low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnectivity across clustered nodes. The server omits discrete GPU acceleration and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its hardware profile exclusively toward compute and local disk throughput.

From an efficiency perspective, the provision of 15.8 TB of bundled NVMe storage and dedicated core allocation allows high operational density for disk-bound and cluster-distributed tasks, bypassing the cost and latency overhead of separate network storage. The absence of hardware accelerators makes it cost-effective for pure CPU-bound mathematical and storage-heavy jobs rather than deep learning training. HB368-96rs_v5 is appropriate for tightly coupled high-performance computing, computational fluid dynamics, large-scale extract-transform-load (ETL) routines, seismic data analysis, and I/O-intensive database engines.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368-96rs_v5 is a dedicated high-performance computing instance built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The configuration provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 448 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation of approximately 4.67 GB of RAM per core. For high-throughput local data processing, the instance integrates 15,875 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It also incorporates RDMA capability for low-latency node-to-node networking and supports Premium Storage configurations. The hardware does not feature integrated GPU acceleration, focusing entirely on CPU-driven parallel processing and fast disk throughput. This combination of dense local solid-state storage, dedicated CPU resources, and RDMA networking yields strong resource efficiency for data-heavy cluster computing without incurring accelerator overhead. The server fits distributed scientific simulations, computational fluid dynamics, large-scale financial modeling, big data batch processing, and high-throughput database workloads.
